name: countless stones

attributes.attribute: a Scottish and British folk motif
put a loaf on each stone, the loaves vanished

sources: Grinsell, Leslie V. Folklore of Prehistoric Sites in Britain. London: David & Charles, 1976, 63.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The countless stones is a folkloric motif found across Scotland and Britain. A common tale says a person can never count all the stones that stand in a ring. Bad luck struck anyone who tried to count them, most of all the stones of Stonehenge and Stanton Drew. In some tellings a baker placed a loaf of bread on each stone in turn to break the spell. The loaves vanished as he went around the ring, so the stones stayed uncounted.

okr.objective: Countless stones is a British folk motif about stone circles that cannot be counted.
key_results: The tale says one can never count all the stones in a ring.
